- uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

Node's default test-file matching: "If no paths are provided, the test runner searches the current working directory recursively for files matching the default patterns": `**/*.test.{cjs,mjs,js}`, `**/*-test.{...}`, `**/*_test.{...}`? Actually the documented patterns are:

- `**/*.test.{cjs,mjs,js}`
- `**/*-test.{cjs,mjs,js}`
- `**/*_test.{cjs,mjs,js}` (maybe)
- `**/test-*.{...}`
- `**/test.{...}`
- `**/test/**/*.{cjs,mjs,js}` — yes! "files within a test directory" is one of the patterns.

From Node docs (v22): "the test runner will run all files matching: `**/*.test.?(c|m)js`, `**/*-test.?(c|m)js`, `**/*_test.?(c|m)js`, `**/test-*.?(c|m)js`, `**/test.?(c|m)js`, `**/test/**/*.?(c|m)js`". Yes — `**/test/**/*.?(c|m)js` includes test/mock-serve.mjs and test/conformance.test.mjs.

---
tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart
---

# pr-1228: feat(1101): Agent Wire Protocol v1 — web reference client (sdk/web), conformance runner, browser example

## Description

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)
- **Conformance runner** `sdk/web/test/conformance.test.mjs` (node:test, 9 tests): parses EVERY golden event fixture with the pinned classification, reproduces EVERY pinned command frame from the semantic payload, handshake/negotiation cases, version gate, NDJSON incl. Cyrillic UTF-8, E4 redaction.
- **CI hook** `test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` — `dart test` invokes `node --test`, so the Dart server and the TS client drift-proof each other in the existing CI gate (AC4/UT-3); loud failure when node is missing.
- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.
- **`sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`** — dependency-free scripted engine (Node, RFC6455 over raw TCP) for local smoke without fa.
- `sdk/web/README.md` (connect/prompt/approvals, AC6) + `docs/wire-protocol.md` §7 updated to reflect the shipped client.

## Verified

- `node --test` in sdk/web: 9/9 pass; `dist` builds; example script parses.
- `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean on the new test; `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` passes (runs the node suite).
- **Browser E2E** (headless Chromium ↔ mock engine): handshake → `connected (protocol v1)`; Cyrillic streamed text rendered mojibake-free (`Привет мир — готово`); tool lifecycle lines; the engine received exactly the golden-shaped frames — `approval_response{approve_once}`, `ask_response{selected:[Postgres]},{freeText:none}`, `secret_response{granted:true,value}` — and the secret value never appears in the page.

## Remaining (slices 3+ of #1101)

- `sdk/ios`, `sdk/android`, `sdk/macos`, `sdk/rn` clients + their conformance runners (same fixture corpus).
- EMB-0/1/2 embedded-runtime spikes (OQ1a) and the shared scripted-scenario fixture divergence guard.
- Downgrade filter (E5) gets real teeth when a second live version exists; today v1 is the only live version by design.

Session JSONL untouched, no `lib/` changes (AC7): this slice is purely additive — `sdk/`, one test, one docs line.

blocks.text:
The background job has printed nothing beyond the grep result and node version after ~10 minutes — so `node --test` in sdk/web is HANGING. This confirms the BLOCKING bug: `node --test` picks up `test/mock-serve.mjs` (because node --test's default pattern includes all `.mjs` files inside `test/` directories), starts the HTTP/WebSocket server on 127.0.0.1:8091, and never exits. This means `dart test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` (Process.runSync 'node --test') will also hang forever → CI timeout.

Wait — let me verify carefully. Node's default test-file matching: "If no paths are provided, the test runner searches the current working directory recursively for files matching the default patterns": `**/*.test.{cjs,mjs,js}`, `**/*-test.{...}`, `**/*_test.{...}`? Actually the documented patterns are:

- `**/*.test.{cjs,mjs,js}`
- `**/*-test.{cjs,mjs,js}`
- `**/*_test.{cjs,mjs,js}` (maybe)
- `**/test-*.{...}`
- `**/test.{...}`
- `**/test/**/*.{cjs,mjs,js}` — yes! "files within a test directory" is one of the patterns.

From Node docs (v22): "the test runner will run all files matching: `**/*.test.?(c|m)js`, `**/*-test.?(c|m)js`, `**/*_test.?(c|m)js`, `**/test-*.?(c|m)js`, `**/test.?(c|m)js`, `**/test/**/*.?(c|m)js`". Yes — `**/test/**/*.?(c|m)js` includes test/mock-serve.mjs and test/conformance.test.mjs.

So mock-serve.mjs runs as a "test" — it has no tests, but it starts a listening server. Node test runner: does the process exit after tests? The runner schedules process exit; I believe `node --test` explicitly calls `process.exit` after completion (in run() it does `exit(code)`)? Hmm — actually I recall node:test's runner does NOT forcibly exit, and there were issues where open handles hang the test runner. Actually in Node 20+, `node --test` will report "tests complete" but the process stays alive if handles remain open... There are GitHub issues: "node --test hangs when a server is listening". Yes, issue nodejs/node#51251 etc. — open handles cause hang since the test runner doesn't force-exit.

Our empirical evidence: the job is still running after 10+ minutes. Let me double-check the job status — maybe it's actually the `grep -n` before... no, grep printed. The `node --test` is hanging. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone.   - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)

- **CI hook** `test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` — `dart test` invokes `node --test`, so the Dart server and the TS client drift-proof each other in the existing CI gate (AC4/UT-3); loud failure when node is missing.
- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.

- EMB-0/1/2 embedded-runtime spikes (OQ1a) and the shared scripted-scenario fixture divergence guard.
- Downgrade filter (E5) gets real teeth when a second live version exists; today v1 is the only live version by design.

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)
- **Conformance runner** `sdk/web/test/conformance.test.mjs` (node:test, 9 tests): parses EVERY golden event fixture with the pinned classification, reproduces EVERY pinned command frame from the semantic payload, handshake/negotiation cases, version gate, NDJSON incl. Cyrillic UTF-8, E4 redaction.

- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.

- `sdk/web/README.md` (connect/prompt/approvals, AC6) + `docs/wire-protocol.md` §7 updated to reflect the shipped client.

- `node --test` in sdk/web: 9/9 pass; `dist` builds; example script parses.

- `sdk/ios`, `sdk/android`, `sdk/macos`, `sdk/rn` clients + their conformance runners (same fixture corpus).

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)

- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.

🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.

🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: guard the `parseLine` null before `handle`**

`parseLine` returns `null` for blank/whitespace lines by design. `handle(null, …)` then throws a `TypeError` (`frame.kind`), which the outer `try/catch` surfaces as a protocol error and **closes the socket**. A stray blank line (some proxies/servers emit keep-alive newlines; a future server-side change could too) would tear down a healthy session with a scary error banner.

```js
const frame = parseLine(e.data);
if (frame) handle(frame, offered.versions);
```

The loud `catch` stays — it just gets reserved for real protocol failures.

💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. Wrap the decode in the same try/catch that already produces the 404.

💡 **SUGGESTION: drop the redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate**

```ts
if (
  kind.startsWith('tool_') &&
  (kind === 'tool_execution_start' || … )
)
```

The explicit kind list already fully determines the set — `startsWith('tool_')` adds a second, wider condition that can never change the outcome (e.g. a hypothetical future `tool_foo` kind passes `startsWith` but fails the inner list, and `tool_pairing_repair` — a known kind with no `toolCallId` requirement — fails `startsWith` semantics either way). Simplify to the plain disjunction, or hoist the five kinds into a `TOOL_ID_KINDS` readonly array and use `.includes(kind)`, matching the style of `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`/`REQUEST_EVENT_KINDS` above. Pure readability; no behavior change.

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)

- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)

- **CI hook** `test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` — `dart test` invokes `node --test`, so the Dart server and the TS client drift-proof each other in the existing CI gate (AC4/UT-3); loud failure when node is missing.
- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.

- EMB-0/1/2 embedded-runtime spikes (OQ1a) and the shared scripted-scenario fixture divergence guard.
- Downgrade filter (E5) gets real teeth when a second live version exists; today v1 is the only live version by design.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. Wrap the decode in the same try/catch that already produces the 404.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Wait — let me verify carefully. Node's default test-file matching: "If no paths are provided, the test runner searches the current working directory recursively for files matching the default patterns": `**/*.test.{cjs,mjs,js}`, `**/*-test.{...}`, `**/*_test.{...}`? Actually the documented patterns are:

- `**/*.test.{cjs,mjs,js}`
- `**/*-test.{cjs,mjs,js}`
- `**/*_test.{cjs,mjs,js}` (maybe)
- `**/test-*.{...}`
- `**/test.{...}`
- `**/test/**/*.{cjs,mjs,js}` — yes! "files within a test directory" is one of the patterns.

From Node docs (v22): "the test runner will run all files matching: `**/*.test.?(c|m)js`, `**/*-test.?(c|m)js`, `**/*_test.?(c|m)js`, `**/test-*.?(c|m)js`, `**/test.?(c|m)js`, `**/test/**/*.?(c|m)js`". Yes — `**/test/**/*.?(c|m)js` includes test/mock-serve.mjs and test/conformance.test.mjs.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. Wrap the decode in the same try/catch that already produces the 404.

Review complete. All artifacts written to `outputs/`.

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES

### 🚨 Blocking (2 — same root cause, two call sites)
**`node --test` hangs forever — verified empirically.** Bare `node --test` (node ≥22) auto-discovers every `.mjs` under `**/test/**`, so it executes `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs` — a server that starts listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never exits. On this checkout (node v22.23.3): all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the runner idles indefinitely (still alive after 15+ min; `ps` confirmed `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child; killing it let the runner finish). Since `Process.runSync` has no timeout and CI bin-packs unknown test files into shards, both the Dart conformance hook (`test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart:22`) and `npm test` (`sdk/web/package.json:9`) will hang CI until job timeout — contradicting the PR's "Verified" claim. Fix: `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs`.

### 💡 Suggestions (4)
- Add a `timeout` to the `Process.runSync` node invocation
- Example `index.html:73`: `parseLine` returns `null` on blank lines → `handle(null)` throws and kills a healthy socket; guard it
- `mock-serve.mjs:119`: static server serves the entire cwd (resolve against an explicit root); `decodeURIComponent` can throw `URIError` → unhandled rejection crashes the mock
- `wire-client.ts:320`: redundant `kind.startsWith('tool_')` predicate — the explicit kind list already decides

### 📦 General note
`sdk/web/dist/` (build output) is not in `.gitignore` — worth adding so the type-stripped bundle is never accidentally committed.

The conformance-pinned-against-golden-fixtures architecture itself is solid, and the client faithfully mirrors the Dart contract (`negotiate`, canonical command shapes, E3 passthrough, E4 redaction all match `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. Wrap the decode in the same try/catch that already produces the 404.

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES

### 🚨 Blocking (2 — same root cause, two call sites)
**`node --test` hangs forever — verified empirically.** Bare `node --test` (node ≥22) auto-discovers every `.mjs` under `**/test/**`, so it executes `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs` — a server that starts listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never exits. On this checkout (node v22.23.3): all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the runner idles indefinitely (still alive after 15+ min; `ps` confirmed `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child; killing it let the runner finish). Since `Process.runSync` has no timeout and CI bin-packs unknown test files into shards, both the Dart conformance hook (`test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart:22`) and `npm test` (`sdk/web/package.json:9`) will hang CI until job timeout — contradicting the PR's "Verified" claim. Fix: `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs`.

### 💡 Suggestions (4)
- Add a `timeout` to the `Process.runSync` node invocation
- Example `index.html:73`: `parseLine` returns `null` on blank lines → `handle(null)` throws and kills a healthy socket; guard it
- `mock-serve.mjs:119`: static server serves the entire cwd (resolve against an explicit root); `decodeURIComponent` can throw `URIError` → unhandled rejection crashes the mock
- `wire-client.ts:320`: redundant `kind.startsWith('tool_')` predicate — the explicit kind list already decides

### 📦 General note
`sdk/web/dist/` (build output) is not in `.gitignore` — worth adding so the type-stripped bundle is never accidentally committed.

The conformance-pinned-against-golden-fixtures architecture itself is solid, and the client faithfully mirrors the Dart contract (`negotiate`, canonical command shapes, E3 passthrough, E4 redaction all match `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. ## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES

### 🚨 Blocking (2 — same root cause, two call sites)
**`node --test` hangs forever — verified empirically.** Bare `node --test` (node ≥22) auto-discovers every `.mjs` under `**/test/**`, so it executes `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs` — a server that starts listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never exits. On this checkout (node v22.23.3): all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the runner idles indefinitely (still alive after 15+ min; `ps` confirmed `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child; killing it let the runner finish). Since `Process.runSync` has no timeout and CI bin-packs unknown test files into shards, both the Dart conformance hook (`test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart:22`) and `npm test` (`sdk/web/package.json:9`) will hang CI until job timeout — contradicting the PR's "Verified" claim. Fix: `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs`.

### 💡 Suggestions (4)
- Add a `timeout` to the `Process.runSync` node invocation
- Example `index.html:73`: `parseLine` returns `null` on blank lines → `handle(null)` throws and kills a healthy socket; guard it
- `mock-serve.mjs:119`: static server serves the entire cwd (resolve against an explicit root); `decodeURIComponent` can throw `URIError` → unhandled rejection crashes the mock
- `wire-client.ts:320`: redundant `kind.startsWith('tool_')` predicate — the explicit kind list already decides

### 📦 General note
`sdk/web/dist/` (build output) is not in `.gitignore` — worth adding so the type-stripped bundle is never accidentally committed.

The conformance-pinned-against-golden-fixtures architecture itself is solid, and the client faithfully mirrors the Dart contract (`negotiate`, canonical command shapes, E3 passthrough, E4 redaction all match `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30) `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed). - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges. # GitHub tracker comment Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every construct must render natively on GitHub. - Headings: `##`, `###` - Bullets: `- item` - Numbered lists: `1. item` - Bold: `**text**` - Inline code: `` `code` `` - Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`) - Link: `[text](url)` - Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row) Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks, no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no `{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable. **IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues, get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER` (the composite key form works directly). ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SAFETY["CLI command safety"] S1["One simple executable command at a time"] S2["DMTools rejects shell metacharacters"] end subgraph FORBIDDEN["NEVER USE"] F1["Pipes: |"] F2["Redirection: > < 2>/dev/null"] F3["Chaining: ; && ||"] F4["Substitution: backticks, $(), ${...}"] end subgraph EXAMPLES["Instead"] E1["find ... | head -20"] --> E1a["run: find ..."] E2["cmd1 && cmd2"] --> E2a["run: cmd1"] --> E2b["then: cmd2"] E3["Complex logic"] --> E3a["Write script file, run script as single command"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source?
